<?php

class InputReader {
    private $stream;
    private $buffer;
    private $seek;

    public function __construct($stream) {
        $this->stream = $stream;
        $this->buffer = null;
        $this->seek = 0;
    }

    public function nextString() {
        return fgets($this->stream);
    }

    public function nextInt32() {
        return (int)$this->readNextToken();
    }

    private function readNextToken() {
        if ($this->buffer === null || $this->seek >= count($this->buffer)) {
            $this->seek = 0;
            $this->buffer = $this->nextSplitStrings();
        }

        return $this->buffer[$this->seek++];
    }

    public function nextInt64() {
        return (int)$this->readNextToken();
    }

    public function readArrayOfInt32() {
        return $this->readArray(function($s) {
            return (int)$s;
        });
    }

    public function readArrayOfInt64() {
        return $this->readArray(function($s) {
            return (int)$s;
        });
    }

    public function nextSplitStrings() {
        $line = $this->nextString();
        return array_values(array_filter(explode(' ', $line), function($token) {
            return $token !== '';
        }));
    }

    public function readArray($func) {
        $tokens = $this->nextSplitStrings();
        return array_map($func, $tokens);
    }

    public function readArrayFromString($func, $str) {
        $tokens = array_values(array_filter(explode(' ', $str), function($token) {
            return $token !== '';
        }));
        return array_map($func, $tokens);
    }

    public function dispose() {
        fclose($this->stream);
    }
}

class Task {
    private $sr;
    private $sw;

    public function __construct(InputReader $sr, $sw) {
        $this->sr = $sr;
        $this->sw = $sw;
    }

    public function solve() {
        $n = $this->sr->nextInt32();
        $str = trim($this->sr->nextString());
        $max = 0;
        $len = strlen($str);
        for ($i = 0; $i < $len; $i++) {
            if (ctype_lower($str[$i])) {
                $set = [];
                for ($j = $i; $j < $len; $j++) {
                    if (ctype_lower($str[$j])) {
                        $set[$str[$j]] = true;
                    } else {
                        break;
                    }
                }
                $max = max(count($set), $max);
            }
        }

        fwrite($this->sw, $max . "\n");
    }

    public function dispose() {
        $this->sr->dispose();
    }
}

$sw = STDOUT;

$task = new Task($sr, $sw);

source_data.prob_desc_description: Polycarp loves lowercase letters and dislikes uppercase ones. Once he got a string s consisting only of lowercase and uppercase Latin letters.Let A be a set of positions in the string. Let's call it pretty if following conditions are met:  letters on positions from A in the string are all distinct and lowercase;  there are no uppercase letters in the string which are situated between positions from A (i.e. there is no such j that s[j] is an uppercase letter, and a1 < j < a2 for some a1 and a2 from A). Write a program that will determine the maximum number of elements in a pretty set of positions.
source_data.prob_desc_output_spec: Print maximum number of elements in pretty set of positions for string s.
source_data.prob_desc_input_spec: The first line contains a single integer n (1 ≤ n ≤ 200) — length of string s. The second line contains a string s consisting of lowercase and uppercase Latin letters.
source_data.prob_desc_notes: NoteIn the first example the desired positions might be 6 and 8 or 7 and 8. Positions 6 and 7 contain letters 'a', position 8 contains letter 'b'. The pair of positions 1 and 8 is not suitable because there is an uppercase letter 'B' between these position.In the second example desired positions can be 7, 8 and 11. There are other ways to choose pretty set consisting of three elements.In the third example the given string s does not contain any lowercase letters, so the answer is 0.
